description: Plan, draft, and revise competitive research grant applications — research plans, mentoring/career-development plans, budget justifications, abstracts, and specific aims. Invoke whenever writing or strengthening a grant proposal, auditing a draft against a funder's guidelines or review criteria, framing significance/innovation, responding to reviewer feedback, or preparing community-engaged/CBPR research budgets — e.g. "is this responsive to the funder", "review my research plan", "strengthen my mentoring plan", "check this against the guidelines". Built from real William T. Grant (WTG) Scholars application work; generalizes to NIH, NSF, and foundation career/research awards. Disambiguation: this skill owns proposal STRATEGY, STRUCTURE, and funder alignment — it wins on structure for proposals because the funder mandates the section order, whereas information-architecture is the skill for structuring content whose shape is yours to decide; for sentence-level voice and word choice pair with a scholarly-voice/academic-writing skill if you keep one; for study design, frameworks, and IRB substance use research-methods; for non-technical/business audiences use plain-language.
